entry_points.text: Utimes dispatch selects fd handling for null pathname with valid dirfd else pathname handling, short-circuiting on dual omit; legacy aliases normalize to a two-entry pair with fixed defaults; xattr set, get, list and remove entries adapt over at-variants with fixed directory and follow behavior, bounding extensible structs and unpacking value, size and flags.

Dentry hooks cover revalidation, hash, compare, delete, init, release, prune, inode release, render, automount, transit, stacking and alias locking; accessors report count and test whiteout, special and file states.
Debug aux creation selects full versus short constructors; numeric helper encodes a number into the aux pointer with decoder.

exports.text: Compat timerfd shims translate 32-bit timer specs to native form, delegate to shared helpers, report copy faults as memory faults and write back only on success.
Generic list walks attribute handlers, skips entries without prefix or rejected by visibility, packs survivors into caller buffer and returns used length or first fault.
Block helpers offer sync read, prefetch, alloc-or-fetch, cache-only lookup in blocking and nonblocking forms, plus batch read and prefetch.
Headers publish config callbacks, dentry descriptors, debug helpers, quota descriptors and loader parameters for cross-file use.

hazards.text: Name import rejects empty or overlong names; list and removal reject bad flags, report missing descriptors and retry only staleness; user pointers are untrusted with faults on copy failure and no partial mutation.

Buffers need reference discipline with ordered completion; null inode marks negative and must not be dereferenced; disconnected entries may need splicing; disabled debug calls return error pointers testable only with error-pointer checks.

invariants.text: Path update allows only nofollow and empty-path, follows symlinks iff nofollow absent and retries once on staleness; descriptor update allows no flags; timeval microseconds are range-checked then scaled to nanoseconds.

Attribute permission gates trusted on privilege, limits user by file kind with sticky-dir ownership check and defers otherwise; user-prefix probe fails closed; unpermissioned set prefers filesystem handler else security store for security names; locked set and remove require permission, security authorization and delegation release; capability values pass mount-aware conversion.

Security-name get queries security store with distinct probe versus copy handling, falling through only when unclaimed; allocating getter probes length, grows zeroed buffer, fills and returns length; listing uses filesystem op else security names, truncating oversized requests and mapping over-ceiling range failure to too-big.

Set copy allows only create and replace flags and bounded values; ACL names divert to dedicated helpers; path, file and at-based operations allow only nofollow and empty-path, treat null pathname with valid descriptor as file operation with mount write hold and audit, and retry once on staleness.

Small-attribute alloc fails on null value or size wrap; free tolerates null with RCU variant; identity hashes parent address plus name with auto-shrink; add inserts into lazily allocated hash then RCU list, bounded variant pre-charges limits and refunds on failure.

Buffer helpers offer set, clear and test with test-and-set and test-and-clear; page accessor needs private marker, indexed walk takes a reference; mapping records placement; forget tolerates null, fallbacks are no-ops or success, migration hooks are null.
Config helpers return name, cast node to group with null tolerance, forward refcounts and queue default subgroups; quota depth expands fanout until spanning 32-bit space.

Debug attribute macro builds ops table from get, set, format and signedness; disabled lookup and creation report missing-device, removals and typed creators are no-ops, file get succeeds and put is no-op.
Routed fragments rely on external container, mapping, barrier, bit, error, string, hash, list and table helpers owned elsewhere.

locks.text: Attribute set and remove hold inode lock across authorization and mutation, release before delegation wait and repeat after success.
Misc registry uses a spin guard, sibling I/O serializes on per-page guard, small attributes use RCU ordering with hashed-table discipline.
Subsystem mutex guards embedded group with unlocked helper adding no locking; dentry flags use entry spinlock with normal versus nested classes.

state_machines.text: Delegation loops attempt-under-lock and wait-without-lock until non-delegated result; path lookup repeats with revalidation on staleness, else accepts first outcome.
Buffer lifecycle covers validity, dirtiness, access, submission, placement variants, async activity, boundaries, failures, quiet handling, hints, deferred completion, migration and a private floor.
Entry kind is one of miss, whiteout, directory, autodir, regular, special or symlink; whiteout halts traversal, autodir presumes automount.

structs.text: Sort key holds parent list pointer plus name pointer; buffer descriptor holds state, ring link, page union, block location, device, private pointer, linkage, count and completion guard.

Execution block holds address anchors, identity, control bits, file refs, credentials, counts, names, limits and scratch; misc helper holds roster and interpreter choice; handler links into roster with load and optional dump; registry pairs hash table with guard and switch.

Config node holds name, refcount, links, type and dentry; type pins owner with ops and attribute arrays; group embeds node with rosters and links; attributes expose callbacks with size for binary; item and group ops manage lifecycle and visibility; subsystem pairs group with mutex.

Name descriptor pairs hash, length and name with combined view; entry holds flags, sequence, chain, parent, names, inode pointer and inline storage, plus ops, owner, time, private data, lock-count, recency and family links with tail union for alias, lookup, RCU or waiters; snapshot copies descriptor with inline bytes.

Blob, reg, regset, array, short ops, automount and cancellation descriptors hold pointers, counts and callbacks; quota table offers conversion plus ownership test with control block for sizing and depth; FDPIC parameters bundle headers, tables, addresses, stack request, bases and flags.

Core-name ceiling 128; stack selectors 0, 1, 2; exec flags at bits 0, 2, 3, 4 with masks 1, 4, 8, 16; per-page buffer ceiling is page size over 512; config-name length 20; dentry bits 0-11 cover ops and lifecycle, 12-18 cover rename, watch, killed, mounted, automount, transit and LRU with managed mask, 19-21 encode 7 entry types, 22-27 cover nokey, real, par-lookup, cursor, norcu and persistent; inline name has 3 word-count alternatives with byte overlay.

Quota credits are 4, 2, 0, 6 generic, 1, 1, 0, 2 for v1, v2 reuses generic; FDPIC mask 0x0f with 0-3 arrangements plus 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80000000, with 32- or 64-bit name mappings and property alignment 4 and 8; each header has an inclusion sentinel; binfmt, buffer and configfs guards allow repeated inclusion.
